data.exact_reserve_text: Estimate of ultimate gross claims costs*:

named_events.loss_description: significantly impacted business activity during 2020 with uncertainty continuing to remain into 2021. Ongoing pandemic restrictions have led to decreased business activity in many segments. Many businesses have decreased fleet sizes or laid-up vehicles and new car sales declined as car dealerships closed, driving lower premium income. Although written premiums have been adversely affected in the year owing to the ongoing pandemic, the overall underwriting performance has improved significantly compared to the prior year. A major improvement in net loss ratio (by 10.1%) was reported from prior year reflecting the improvements made in risk selection and product mix, but predominantly from the benefits on claims frequencies due to the restrictions imposed to limit the spread of COVID-19 which reduced road and vehicle usage. Claims frequencies fell dramatically during the first lockdown in March and April; and then again to a lesser extent in the second lockdown in November. This offset higher claims costs where the increase in used car prices as new car sales have fallen is driving inflation in the cost of replacing written-off vehicles.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a gross prior year reserve release of GBP 1.5 million, primarily driven by favorable claims development across various underwriting years up to 2018. This release is also influenced by the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, which led to reduced claims frequencies due to lockdown measures and decreased road usage. The movement was calculated from the gross claims development triangle, as the explicit 'Movement in prior accident year's provision' note appears to be net of reinsurance.
raw_causal_phrases: overall underwriting performance has improved significantly compared to the prior year. A major improvement in net loss ratio (by 10.1%) was reported from prior year reflecting the improvements made in risk selection and product mix, but predominantly from the benefits on claims frequencies due to the restrictions imposed to limit the spread of COVID-19 which reduced road and vehicle usage.

The favourable reserves movements in the recent years meant that although there has not been sufficiently adverse aggregate experience to trigger a recovery, ERS have continued to benefit from the guaranteed interest payments.
data.data_quality_notes: The 'Movement in prior accident year's provision for claims outstanding' (Note 7, page 17) explicitly states 'Net claims release' as its first component, and the total is a sum of these releases (GBP 18.163m). Given the instruction to prioritize gross figures, the prior year development was calculated from the 'Analysis of claims development - gross of reinsurance' triangle (page 13). The Part VII transfer of legacy EEA business mentioned on page 17 is an outflow of liabilities, which could contribute to a release, but its specific impact on the claims development triangle is not quantified.
